technical_and_design_decisions: Extend the existing XD runtime and module conventions rather than introducing a new application framework or programming model.
Implement the Kafka load-generator source and throughput-measuring sink as deployable XD modules using the repository's existing module APIs, configuration, serialization, and lifecycle patterns.
Use Kafka consumer assignment and seek semantics for efficient source offset management, with explicit handling for configured starting offsets and partition-level state.
Build the EC2 image from an automatable base AMI using versioned provisioning scripts, installing Java, Kafka clients, test tooling, and performance-test dependencies.
Use repeatable performance-test scripts and publish throughput results with test topology, message size, concurrency, and runtime parameters.
Use a static GitHub Pages site generated from repository-managed Markdown or equivalent static content, with sections for samples, tutorials, links, benchmarks, and reference architectures.
Treat the Lattice/Diego work as a time-boxed proof of concept that evaluates a pluggable XD runtime SPI, including deployment, lifecycle, resource, and failure-handling concerns.
Use the existing CI system and Windows worker or AMI approach where possible, adding only the scripts and configuration needed to schedule and execute the relevant Windows builds.
assumptions: The specification refers to an existing XD codebase with Kafka source and runtime extension points; the estimate excludes creating XD or Spring Framework from scratch.
Repository access, credentials, cloud accounts, CI administration access, and required third-party licenses are available.
The work is performed by one software developer, and estimates represent hands-on workdays rather than elapsed calendar time.
Existing build, test, packaging, and deployment conventions are sufficiently usable and do not require a major migration.
The EC2 AMI target is a Linux image suitable for Kafka performance testing; Windows CI uses a separately provisioned Windows worker or AMI.
Performance characterization is for a simple stream and a representative finite test matrix, not a full-scale capacity or soak-testing program.
The GitHub Pages site is static and does not require a custom backend, authentication, search service, or extensive visual design.
The Lattice/Diego effort is a prototype and design-validation exercise, not production deployment integration.

CI failure isolation is limited to identifying and documenting remaining failures and applying targeted infrastructure or test fixes; it does not guarantee that every pre-existing failure is resolved.
Code review, normal source-control operations, and ordinary developer documentation are included within the listed activities; major external review or release-management work is excluded.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing XD architecture, Kafka integration, module APIs, build layout, CI configuration, and deployment conventions; define interfaces, configuration, test strategy, and sequencing for the increment.

Create repeatable AMI provisioning scripts and configuration for Java, Kafka client or broker dependencies, performance tools, monitoring utilities, and the packages required by the Kafka performance tests.
Build and launch the AMI, verify installed versions and connectivity, execute a smoke performance test, correct packaging issues, and document image creation and usage.
Implement the source module, including configuration, message generation, partition or topic targeting, lifecycle behavior, error handling, and integration with the existing XD runtime.

activities.activity_name: Source module unit and integration tests
activities.activity_description: Add tests for configuration, generation behavior, lifecycle, serialization, error cases, and execution against a Kafka test environment; update build and module metadata.
Implement the sink module to consume or receive test records, count received messages and bytes, expose throughput measurements, handle lifecycle and errors, and follow existing XD sink conventions.
Add unit and integration tests for record receipt, byte and message counters, reporting behavior, configuration, shutdown, and failure handling.
Correct source offset handling so fetch operations begin at configured or recovered partition offsets, using efficient seek and assignment behavior while preserving normal consumer processing.
Add tests covering initial offsets, multiple partitions, offset boundaries, restart or recovery behavior, missing or invalid offsets, and prevention of unintended scans from the beginning.
Configure scheduled Windows builds, worker or AMI setup, environment variables, dependency installation, build commands, artifact collection, and basic notifications or logs.

activities.activity_name: Windows CI failure isolation and stabilization
activities.activity_description: Run the scheduled builds, classify environment versus product failures, experiment with suitable Windows images or dependencies, apply targeted fixes, and document remaining failures and known limitations.
Create a repeatable source-to-sink benchmark, parameterize message size and load rate as needed, execute representative runs, collect throughput and resource observations, and summarize the results.
Set up the static site structure and publishing workflow, organize samples, tutorials, links, performance benchmarks, and reference architectures, and add navigation and basic validation.

Continue the prototype by implementing or adapting the runtime integration needed to exercise a pluggable SPI, including deployment invocation, lifecycle interactions, configuration, and representative failure paths.
Run the Lattice/Diego prototype, identify scope and risks, compare integration alternatives, and produce a proposed SPI shape and follow-up implementation recommendations.
Integrate source, sink, offset, AMI, benchmark, and CI changes; run relevant unit, integration, packaging, and end-to-end tests; resolve integration defects and update compatibility checks.
Consolidate configuration references, benchmark instructions and results, CI usage, AMI instructions, module examples, known issues, and implementation notes for maintainers and users.
